description:
About the Position

The University of Amsterdam (UvA) advertises a PhD position in political science on militarization and democratic erosion in Latin America. The project examines how the expanding role of armed forces in public life - from public security to infrastructure and emergency governance - interacts with the quality of democratic institutions across Latin American countries, combining comparative analysis, country cases and where relevant quantitative measures of militarization and democratic performance.

The candidate joins the UvA's Department of Political Science, one of Europe's largest and most internationally staffed political science departments, and contributes to research themes on democracy, security and comparative politics. The employment is a salaried four-year PhD position under the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement with a starting salary of EUR 3,204 per month, including the department's doctoral training programme, methods support and conference travel.

Candidate Profile and Application

Applicants hold a research master's degree in political science, international relations, Latin American studies or a related discipline, with strong analytical writing and comparative-research skills; Spanish or Portuguese language ability is an advantage for fieldwork and sources. Applications - CV, transcripts, research statement and references - are submitted through the UvA academic careers portal, and the closing date is 6 November 2026.

Highlights

  • PhD on militarization and democratic erosion in Latin America
  • Comparative and case-based political science research
  • UvA Department of Political Science environment
  • Salaried four-year position (EUR 3,204 - 4,051 per month)
  • Spanish/Portuguese an advantage for fieldwork
  • Closing date: 6 November 2026

About University of Amsterdam

The University of Amsterdam (UvA) is the largest university in the Netherlands and one of Europe's leading research institutions. Its seven faculties span the humanities, social and behavioural sciences, economics and business, law, science, medicine in cooperation with Amsterdam UMC, and dentistry. PhD candidates at the UvA are employed on salaried contracts under the CAO-NU collective agreement, making doctoral research here fully funded. Academic vacancies and doctoral positions are published on the university's academic careers portal with detailed role profiles and application requirements.
